headline: Bharat Semi Raises $24 Million Seed Round to Build AI Image Sensors in India
subheadline: The New Delhi startup, still pre-revenue, says it has design wins with General Atomics and Kaynes Semicon and targets first commercial production in 2027.
body:
• Bharat Semi, a New Delhi semiconductor startup, has raised $24 million in an all-equity seed round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures, TechCrunch reported on November 15.
  • The nearly five-year-old company is pre-revenue. It says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology company General Atomics and India's Kaynes Semicon, and is targeting initial commercial production in 2027.
  • Its programmable image sensors combine image capture, processing and AI on a single chip. Co-founder Vrinda Kapoor said the approach could cut system costs by at least 70% compared with setups using a separate sensor, image signal processor and system-on-chip.
  • Bharat Semi has about 75 employees across India and the United States, including 10 to 12 in Santa Clara, and plans to raise its U.S. headcount to around 20 by mid-2027.

Bharat Semi, an Indian semiconductor startup developing AI-enabled image sensors, has raised $24 million in seed funding as it seeks customers in the United States and other global markets, according to TechCrunch. The all-equity round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures, with participation from Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels and individual investors.

The company plans to use the funding to expand its engineering team, complete product development and bring its sensors to market. It remains pre-revenue, and its sensors are still under development.

Sensors that process what they see

Bharat Semi is developing programmable image sensors that combine image capture, processing and AI capabilities on a single chip, reducing the need to send visual data to separate processors. On its official site, the company argues that moving data between components creates latency, power and cost burdens for drones, robots and other devices with tight power budgets, and that interpreting visual data on the device lets machines act without sending every image elsewhere.

"Our aim here is to move from sensors to sense-making solutions."

— Vrinda Kapoor, co-founder, Bharat Semi, speaking to TechCrunch

The company is targeting smart homes, industrial automation, surveillance and aerospace. Kapoor pointed to air conditioners that could detect when a room is empty and adjust automatically, and drones that could process visual information without more expensive computing hardware elsewhere in the system. Bharat Semi lists consumer electronics, surveillance, robotics, automotive, aerospace and security systems among its target industries.

Timeline to production

The startup's first-generation sensors are already in prototyping. Its second-generation sensors, which will incorporate more advanced AI capabilities, are expected to reach the prototype stage by mid-2027, Kapoor said, with the newer sensors planned to reach customers by the end of 2027. Initial commercial production is targeted for 2027.

Design wins are an early commercial signal, not revenue: the company says General Atomics and Kaynes Semicon have selected its technology for development programs, while the sensors themselves remain under development.

The team behind it

Kapoor, a South Park Commons fellow who earlier worked in healthcare technology, co-founded Bharat Semi in late 2021 with Vinayak Dalmia, the startup's managing director, who previously worked at McKinsey and in private equity. Its chief technology officer, Boyd Fowler, previously held the same role at image-sensor maker OmniVision.

The company has about 75 employees across India and the U.S., including 10 to 12 in its Santa Clara operations spanning engineering and business development, and plans to increase U.S. headcount to around 20 by mid-2027. It has also begun hiring engineers in Europe.

Fabless by design, with a separate fab project

Bharat Semi plans to remain fabless in its image-sensor business, outsourcing chip manufacturing while focusing on semiconductor design and software. The new funding will not be used to finance the semiconductor fabrication project it announced plans for in India in 2024, which involved a technology partnership with the U.S. Space Force. Kapoor said that project remains in development and the startup is working to identify domestic partners that would build and operate the facility.

The round lands as India has committed billions of dollars to build a domestic semiconductor industry and position itself as an alternative manufacturing hub, while the AI boom gives Indian startups an opening to develop specialized chips for global markets.

"It's a story of can we build a global technology company out of India."

— Vrinda Kapoor, co-founder, Bharat Semi, speaking to TechCrunch
diaspora_angle: An Indian-founded chip startup is hiring in Santa Clara and selling to U.S. customers, a concrete example of India-based deep-tech firms building for the American market.

key_takeaways: Bharat Semi raised $24 million in seed funding for AI image sensors.
The startup is targeting initial commercial production in 2027.
Its sensors aim to reduce system costs by at least 70%.
Bharat Semi plans to expand its U.S. workforce to 20 by mid-2027.
The company is pre-revenue and still developing its sensors.
